featured_reviews.name: Jaimeen Bulsara
featured_reviews.review_text: Had a wonderful experience at Ajanta Cinex. This was our second time coming here. Tucked away in a by-lane, very close to the station (if you’re coming by train) as well as ample parking (if you prefer to come by car/bike) it is super convenient to reach. The movie watching experience itself is amazing, it is currently the only single screen theatre with Dolby sound system. Clean, comfortable seating, delicious food options (we tried the momos, pizza, and coffee, along with the usual samosa and popcorn). The freshly made momos and pizza were better than some of the food places we’ve eaten at. Overall a total 5 on 5 experience. Would definitely come again soon.

featured_reviews.name: Jeevan Nagarkar
featured_reviews.review_text: The staff seemed untrained. The theatre was renovated, but cleaning needs attention there was a slight smell inside, not too strong but enough to distract while watching the movie. They should also put clear directions outside the mall since there are two entrances. At one entrance, the watchman was chewing gutka and just threw hand signs when I asked where the theatre was, which didn’t feel professional. Another odd thing was at the last 10 minutes of the movie, the lights were turned on while it was still playing. On the positive side, the ticket prices were low, the seats were good, and the washrooms were clean, so overall 3 stars for that

featured_reviews.review_text:

Otherwise the theatre is good. Seating is comfortable. Food options are ok similar or slightly lower priced than bigger theatres.

featured_reviews.name: nigam sarvaiya
featured_reviews.review_text:
Located conveniently near the National Park in Veena CHSL, Shantivan, Borivali East, Sona Gold Digital Cinema offers a cozy and budget-friendly movie-watching experience for local residents and casual visitors alike.

The theatre may not be as flashy as the big multiplexes, but it holds its charm with a nostalgic feel and a simple setup. The seats are decent and comfortable enough for a casual movie outing, and the sound and picture quality are surprisingly good for the price. It’s a great option for spontaneous plans or watching the latest releases without burning a hole in your pocket.

What stands out is the affordable ticket pricing and convenient location – perfect for locals looking to catch a film without heading to a crowded mall. Staff are polite and helpful, and entry and exit are generally smooth. While the snacks and facilities are basic, they do the job, and cleanliness is maintained reasonably well.

Pros:
- Affordable ticket prices
- Convenient location near National Park
- Decent audio-visual quality
- Friendly staff

Cons:
- Limited screen and seat capacity
- Basic amenities and snack options
- Less suitable for those looking for a premium experience

Overall, Sona Gold Digital Cinema is a reliable neighbourhood theatre that delivers on value. Great for everyday moviegoers and those who appreciate a more laid-back, no-frills cinema outing.

Rating: 3.8/5

featured_reviews.name: Pankaj Powermax
featured_reviews.review_text:
INOX at Thakur Mall in Dahisar is a popular entertainment hub for residents in the Dahisar and Mira Road areas. Located on the 3rd floor of the mall, it is known for being a well-maintained multiplex that offers a premium cinematic experience at relatively competitive prices compared to other major malls in Mumbai.
Screens: The multiplex typically operates 4 screens, featuring both 2D and 3D projection technology.
​Seating: Options range from standard comfortable seating to luxury recliners (Gold Class) for a more relaxed experience.
​Audio/Visual: Equipped with high-quality sound systems, including Dolby Atmos in select halls, and large screens with high-definition picture quality.
​Accessibility: The cinema is equipped with wheelchair facilities and elevator access.
Refreshments: There is a dedicated F&B counter inside INOX serving classic movie snacks like popcorn, nachos, and sandwiches.
​Food Court: Thakur Mall itself has a multi-cuisine food court on the lower floors, offering a wider variety of dining options after the movie.
​Gaming Zone: There is a gaming area located within the mall, making it a good spot for families and children.
If you're visiting on a weekend, it's advisable to book tickets in advance via apps like BookMyShow, as it is a major landmark and can get quite crowded for blockbuster releases.
Safety system is very nice handle nicely .

featured_reviews.review_text: INOX Thakur Mall - Mira Road really impressed me! 🤩 The atmosphere was absolutely fantastic, and I had such a wonderful time. featured_reviews.name: Keval Somaiya
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re someone who enjoys ads more than movies, this theatre is absolutely perfect for you.

Showtime? More like “suggested time.” I’ve been here multiple times, and without fail, every single show starts 20–30 minutes late. Honestly, you could walk in 20 minutes after the scheduled time and still comfortably sit through a full ad marathon before the movie even begins.

At this point, missing a scene here is nearly impossible—not because of great service, but because punctuality clearly isn’t part of the experience.

It’s hard to tell whether the staff is just taking it easy or the management has created some magical, impossible turnaround schedule between shows. Either way, the result is the same: frustration.

A 2-hour movie somehow turns into a 3-hour commitment. Impressive… just not in the way you’d want.

Would not recommend if you value your time.

featured_reviews.review_text: The experience was average. Screen quality is not good with too much dust and thread visible on the screen. featured_reviews.name: Alok Shettigar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Movie Time is just a 10-minute walk from the Dahisar Metro Station, but finding it was a bit of a struggle since there were no signs outside to guide us. Unlike most theatres, there’s no clear entry point, which made things confusing.

The lift situation wasn’t great either—there’s only one, and it barely fits five people, so getting in and out felt like a waiting game. Inside, there’s just one screen, and honestly, the theatre felt more like a small pod. The viewing experience was okay, but the sound quality could have been way better.

Now, let’s talk about the seats—definitely not the most comfortable. Sitting through a long movie was a bit of a task. On the plus side, the food area was clean, but the prices? Almost as high as PVR, which felt a bit much for the overall experience.

One good thing—they have free underground parking for both bikes and cars, which is a rare win in Mumbai!

Overall, if you’re nearby and just want to catch a movie, it works. But if you’re looking for a top-tier cinema experience, this might not be the best pick.

featured_reviews.name: Dhaval Gami
featured_reviews.review_text:
Very disappointed with the management. Every time I visit this theatre, I face the same issue regarding my bike helmet. Visitors arriving on two-wheelers are not allowed to carry helmets inside, yet there is no proper and secure facility provided to keep them. Customers are forced to leave their helmets outside at their own risk.

This is an inconvenience and a basic customer service issue that has remained unresolved despite repeated visits. If the theatre does not allow helmets inside, it should provide a safe and organized storage facility for riders.

I request the management to address this issue seriously and implement a proper solution instead of making customers face the same problem every time.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Sound system and screen size is top notch.
It has 6 auditoriums.
The 6th one has a weird seating arrangement. Even after sitting in H row in 6th Audi, you'll be very close to the screen. The seats are very irritating because there is no mechanism to adjust their position. Your neck will pain and body aches. It really hurts.

featured_reviews.name: a6ixty8
featured_reviews.review_text:
To begin with, finding the theatre was quite confusing. There were no boards, signs, or posters indicating that a theatre was located there. My cab dropped me right in front of the building, but I still couldn’t see any clear markings to confirm I was at the right place.

Next, after completing the ticket check and heading upstairs, I noticed there were very few seats available for waiting. Only about ten people could sit on a sofa, and the rest had to stand until roughly ten minutes before the show began. So, if you arrive early, be prepared to wait standing.

Another issue — (Screen 2) avoid seats D19 and D20 in the upper section. Your view will be blocked by a gypsum board placed directly in front.

The seating overall is not very comfortable, especially for back support. The sound quality was also below expectations, lacking smoothness and clarity.

Like in many theatres, disturbances were present: people searching for seats with mobile flashlights after the movie started, crying babies, phone conversations, latecomers, people recording videos, and vendors distributing popcorn mid-show etc.

Speaking of popcorn — I paid ₹460 for one serving and ₹70 for a half-litre bottle of mineral water. Including my travel, I spent around ₹1,500 just to watch a movie.

Finally, a serious safety concern: when exiting after the show, you must use the stairs. Some steps are partially damaged, making it risky to walk in a crowd. Today, I even witnessed a man fall while carrying a small child because of the broken steps. Please be cautious.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I had the worst cinema experience at PVR Kandivali. To start with, water was literally leaking from the ceiling onto our seats. Instead of fixing the issue, they just threw a flimsy blue plastic sheet over the seats! It felt like sitting in a rundown shack. Some seats had broken cushions, making it incredibly uncomfortable to sit for the entire movie.

On top of that, the AC wasn’t working, and the whole theatre had a horrible damp, musty smell. It felt like they haven’t maintained the place in ages. The icing on the cake? The volume was cranked up so high, it was uncomfortable and borderline painful to sit through the movie. It didn’t enhance the experience, it made it worse.

This is hands down the worst PVR I’ve ever been to. If you’re planning to watch a movie here, do yourself a favor and go elsewhere. Total waste of time and money!

featured_reviews.name: Yeshika Dhandhania
featured_reviews.review_text:
Extremely disappointing experience at PVR INOX. I requested a blanket and was told by the staff that blankets are only available for recliner seats. When I mentioned that I had received one during a previous visit, the staff simply said that the rules had changed.

What made the situation even more frustrating was that I could clearly see guests seated in front of me who were not in recliner seats but had been given blankets. When I pointed this out, the staff changed their response and told me where I could get one from instead. The inconsistent explanations made it seem like the staff either didn’t know the policy or were unwilling to help.

Customer service should be transparent and consistent. If there is a policy, it should be applied equally to all guests. The entire interaction felt unprofessional and left a negative impression of the cinema experience.
